title: 'We have all been sold a lie': Sovereign citizens and their "common lore" | 7NEWS Spotlight
summary: 7NEWS Spotlight on Australian sovereign-citizen groups, their self-styled common-law courts, police killings and families harmed.

assertions.quote: They were galvanized by rage over the pandemic and the police-enforced restrictions imposed in many states
For the record, tax isn't voluntary

verdicts.note: Income tax is compulsory by statute; 'voluntary compliance' refers only to self-assessment.

assertions.quote: motorists do have to provide their identity if police have a legal reason to ask for it

verdicts.note: A driver who refused license, registration and name was removed from the car, arrested and convicted of obstruction, failure to disclose and failure to display; one case.
Review describes refusal and non-cooperation at stops ending in forcible removal from the vehicle and, in one case, an aggravated assault conviction, not release.

assertions.quote: Though they have no legal authority, they'll be serving homemade documents

verdicts.note: Such bodies have no legal standing; their verdicts are unenforceable and acting on them can itself be a crime.
Self-declared courts and marshals are described as vigilante bodies whose leader was jailed; courts refuse OPCA attempts to enforce their beliefs.
Common-law courts only 'purport' to replace state courts; their in-absentia trials and liens work as harassment, not as lawful authority.
FBI describes the self-convened courts' indictments and warrants as fake documents used to harass officials, not instruments with legal authority.

assertions.quote: self-proclaimed sovereign citizen Desi Freeman executes two police officers
Emma and Jerry Martin were sentenced to 30 days in prison.
Whatever the fringe ideology is, you're guaranteed to find someone like-minded on the internet.

verdicts.note: Psychiatric studies cited conclude pseudolaw adherence is extreme political belief reinforced in small introspective social communities; online forums are the main sharing venue described.
Occupants of the OPCAsphere reinforce each other's beliefs by circulating documents, videos and memes; psychologists found the beliefs reinforced in OPCA communities.
Pseudolegal forms are free online, and pseudolegal communities on social media are insular but supportive.
Social scientists describe true believers held in place by conspiratorial and political beliefs 'reinforced in a kind of social echo chamber'.
Review says the ideology spreads via the Internet, especially YouTube with millions of videos; it describes spread, not peer-group reinforcement.
